page: Amazon Web Services c5.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.4 GHz. Hardware vector capabilities include AVX and AVX-512 extensions. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage and requires remote storage such as EBS, while baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps with no GPU accelerators attached.

Benchmark results highlight a notable divergence between single-core and multi-core operations due to its single physical core constraint. Single-threaded metrics show mid-tier capability, with stress-ng single-core reaching 1485.39 and Geekbench single-core scoring 1202.0. Single-threaded gzip compression operates at 25.09 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core and throughput-intensive metrics land in the lowest tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1435.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2322.4, and uncached large block memory read and write bandwidth near 12 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect these limits, recording 1.87 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the c5.large is its low total thread count and limited 4.0 GB memory footprint. While it offers a low barrier to entry within the compute-optimized family for compute-heavy routines, multi-threaded concurrency is heavily restricted by hyper-threading across a solitary physical core. The instance is best suited for lightweight compute jobs, single-threaded batch tasks, small-scale microservices, build nodes with minimal parallel stages, and low-traffic front-end web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.large is an entry-tier compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs running across 1 physical core via Intel Xeon 8275CL silicon at 3.4 GHz. The instance includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Networking delivers a 1 Gbps baseline. Performance evaluations show average single-core output, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1202.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1485.39. Multi-core performance is limited due to the single physical core ceiling, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1435.0 and lower memory throughput across large blocks. The c5.large represents a low-resource entry point into compute-optimized infrastructure, best matched with single-threaded batch routines, small build workers, and lightweight web serving microservices.
